name: Marvin Gaye
hook: The Motown singer who beat Berry Gordy's refusal to release a political album, and who later built his biggest hit on a TR-808 drum machine in Belgium.

blurb.age13: Marvin Gaye was born in Washington, D.C., in 1939. He signed to Motown in 1960, played drums on other people's sessions, and became one of the label's biggest singers. In 1971 he made 'What's Going On', an album about war, racism, police violence and pollution. Motown's boss, Berry Gordy, said it was too political for the radio and would not release it. Gaye refused to record anything else until he did. The album became a huge hit, and after that Gaye produced his own records. In 1982, living in Belgium, he made 'Sexual Healing' using a drum machine, the Roland TR-808, so he could make the music without other musicians. In 1984 he was shot and killed by his father.
blurb.adult: Born in Washington, D.C., on 2 April 1939. Signed to Motown's Tamla in 1960, he worked as a session drummer before his first solo single in 1961, and through the 1960s was one of the label's steadiest hitmakers, including 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine' with Norman Whitfield. Gordy initially refused to release 'What's Going On' (1971) as too political; Gaye withheld further work until it came out, and its success made him one of the first Motown artists to take control of his own production. After tax exile in Europe he signed to Columbia in March 1982 and recorded 'Midnight Love' in Belgium and Germany. 'Sexual Healing', written in Ostend and released on 9 October 1982, was programmed on a TR-808, which he chose because it let him make a record without other musicians or producers. He was shot dead by his father at his parents' house in Los Angeles on 1 April 1984, the day before his 45th birthday.
